en.html:
The Mongol invasions—the <ruby>so-called<rt>so-called</rt></ruby> Genkou. In the early fighting, Mongol warriors overwhelmed those of Yamato. Their machines' superior mobility and their skill in <ruby>formation tactics<rt>formation</rt></ruby> were among the reasons. Their willingness to use poison was said to be another.

A poison that turned a scratch into a grave wound, and finally a fatal one, must have been an effective weapon. Yet even a survey of the world's military history yielded remarkably few examples of its use.

Among peoples without developed civilization, hunting with poison had innumerable precedents. Among the armies of civilized states, however, most examples outside the Yuan Empire belonged to remote antiquity. For warriors in armor, there were virtually none.

Poison ran directly against that peculiar aesthetic possessed by warriors of <ruby>every age<rt>when</rt></ruby> and <ruby>every nation<rt>where</rt></ruby>: their conception of themselves as kings of the battlefield. The contradiction was <ruby>profound<rt>exceedingly</rt></ruby>.

A warrior possessed strength above the multitude. Therefore, a warrior must also be their example. How could such a person steal a victory by the petty expedient of poison?

That sense of <ruby>honor<rt>pride</rt></ruby> ought to have been a good tradition.

This enemy, <ruby>apparently<rt>it appears</rt></ruby>, had none of it.

ja.html:
蒙古襲来――<ruby>所謂<rt>いわゆる</rt></ruby>元寇の折、緒戦において蒙古側の
武者は大和武者を圧倒したが、その理由は蒙古の騎体
が運動性に優れていた事、<ruby>編隊戦術<rt>フォーメーション</rt></ruby>に長けていた事等
の他に、毒の使用を躊躇わなかった事もあったと云う。

　わずかな掠り傷を重傷、遂には致命傷へ至らしめる
毒はさぞ有効な兵器であったことだろう。
　……しかし、世界軍史を紐解いて総覧しても、その
使用例は決して多くないのが実情だった。

　未開民族の間で狩猟に用いられた例なら無数にある。
だが仮にも文明国家の軍隊が使用した例となると、元
帝国以外は殆どが遥か遠き古代史の範疇だ。
　増して武者の使用例となると絶無である。

　それは毒という物が、<ruby>何時<rt>いつ</rt></ruby>の時代<ruby>何処<rt>どこ</rt></ruby>の国家の武者
にも必ず存在した特有の――戦場の王者としての――
美意識に、真っ向から刃向かうこと<ruby>甚<rt>はなは</rt></ruby>だしかったから
であろう。

　武者は衆に優れた力を持ち、故に衆の模範とならね
ばならなかった。
　その武者がどうして、毒物など用いて姑息に勝利を
盗んだりできようものか？

　そうした意識は武者の<ruby>矜持<rt>プライド</rt></ruby>であり、良き伝統である
筈だった。
　
　それを――かの敵騎は持ち合わせていないと<ruby>思<rt>おぼ</rt></ruby>しい。

en.html:
I was no expert either, but I possessed a little miscellaneous knowledge. Poisons came in many kinds. From the symptoms, I could probably exclude those that acted on organs and those that destroyed the tissue they touched.

That left poisons which disabled the body by damaging the blood, or neurotoxins which attacked the nerves and caused paralysis...

If I could distinguish those two, perhaps I could identify this one.

Perhaps that was merely an illusion produced by my own retreating spirits. The increased speed and force of the charge, however, were real enough and coming straight at me.
en.text:
The balance I had thought settled overturned with remarkable ease. I was cornered; the enemy was visibly encouraged. Its body even seemed a size larger.

Perhaps that was merely an illusion produced by my own retreating spirits. The increased speed and force of the charge, however, were real enough and coming straight at me.

ja.html:
定まったかに思われた勝負の趨勢はあっさりと覆り、
俺は窮地に立たされ、敵は見るからに勢いづいている。
　体躯が一回り大きくなったようにも見えた。

　それは俺の心理的後退が見せた幻覚に過ぎなかった
のかもしれない。
　しかし、突撃の速度と勢威の増大は目前に差し迫る
現実だった。

en.html:
The enemy's wild cries had finally ceased to resemble words. Whether from extreme excitement or some other cause, I did not know, and it was no concern of mine.

Its blade was my concern. How was I to weather that weight—and the poison with it?

For now, defense must take priority over attack. There was, of course, such a conception as <ruby>attacking in order to defend<rt>・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>...

In either case, the available means fell into two broad classes.

<ruby>Sword technique<rt>overt technique</rt></ruby>—or <ruby>hidden arts<rt>covert technique</rt></ruby>.

ja.html:
敵の狂声は遂に言葉の体裁さえ失っている。
　極度の興奮のためか、それ以外の理由によるものか、
それはわからないし知った事でもない。

　対処すべきは敵騎の刃だけだ。
　重厚にして毒をも含むそれを如何に凌ごう。

　今はひとまず攻めよりも守りに専心せねばならない。
　無論、<ruby>守るために攻める<rt>・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>という発想も有ろうが……。

　いずれにせよ手立ては大別して二種だ。
　<ruby>太刀業<rt>おもてわざ</rt></ruby>か、それとも――<ruby>裏業<rt>うらわざ</rt></ruby>か。
